texts.li: [Shooting,lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, an archer who has won every contest from here to the coast, has heard that {A_nameDef} is a good shot. {X_nameDef} proposes a friendly match at straw targets, best of ten.

[Shooting,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a marksman with a bag of medals and an ego to match, wants to shoot tin cans against {A_nameDef}, the colony's best shot. It's a friendly match, and the colony can put silver on it if it likes.

[Melee] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a wrestler built like a door, is touring the settlements looking for anyone willing to try a fall in a ring drawn in the dirt, with no weapons and no hard feelings. The colony's champion would be {A_nameDef}.

[Crafting] {X_nameDef}, a traveling artisan of {FACTION}, says {X_possessive} work is the finest in the region and would like to prove it against {A_nameDef}'s. Both get the same materials and the same time, and the onlookers judge.

[Artistic] {X_nameDef}, a wandering artist of {FACTION}, has heard about {A_nameDef}'s work and doesn't believe a word of it. {X_nameDef} proposes one piece each, made in a single afternoon, with the colony as judge.
[Cooking] {X_nameDef}, a traveling cook of {FACTION} who claims to have fed kings, challenges {A_nameDef} to a cook-off. They'll share one kitchen for an afternoon, and whoever eats gets a vote.
[Social] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a talker known up and down the roads, challenges the colony to a public debate. {A_nameDef} would speak for the colony.
[Animals] {X_nameDef}, a drover of {FACTION}, swears no one can handle a stubborn animal like {X_pronoun} can, and challenges {A_nameDef} to prove otherwise.

[Intellectual] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} challenges the colony's sharpest mind, {A_nameDef}, to a contest of riddles and puzzles. The loser buys the drinks, unless the colony wants to put real silver on it.

[Plants] {X_nameDef}, a gardener of {FACTION}, has heard about the colony's fields and wants to test {A_nameDef}'s eye for seed, soil and sprout against {X_possessive} own. The onlookers will decide who's better.

li.label: Accept: {COUNT} silver on {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The challenge is on, with silver riding on it. It starts in a couple of hours, and word is already going around.

li.label: Accept, for honor only
li.outcome: The challenge is on, for bragging rights only. It starts in a couple of hours.

li.label: Decline politely
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs, says something about cowards that {X_pronoun} probably means as a joke, and moves on.

li.label: Accept, and lay on food for the onlookers
li.outcome: The challenge is on, for honor, and there's food on the tables for anyone who comes to watch. {FACTION} will hear what a good day it was.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] The challenge is on, with bread and roast on trestles for the crowd. It feels more like a fair than a contest, and {X_nameDef} seems to like that.
[summer] Tables in the yard, food for anyone who wants it, and a contest at the end of it. {X_nameDef} has already eaten twice.

titles.li: A beast out of the stories

texts.li: Travelers have talked about it for weeks, and now it's here. {BEAST}, an old {THING} out of the stories, huge and scarred, is roaming the colony's land. It doesn't go looking for trouble, but it fights back hard when hunted. Whoever brings it down will be talked about for years. It will move on in a few days.

[lowtech] Hunters tell stories about {BEAST}, an old {THING} that has outlived every spear ever thrown at it. Now it's wandering the colony's land. {A_nameDef} has already been out to look at it from a distance. It will move on in a few days, whether anyone tries their luck or not.

[!lowtech] An old {THING} that trappers on the road call {BEAST} has wandered onto the colony's land. Bullets have bounced off it before. It has never bothered anyone who left it alone, and it will be gone in a few days. {A_nameDef} is already cleaning a weapon.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, one of the colony's guests, takes {A_nameDef} aside. {X_nameDef} has an old, creased map that shows a cache buried out on the colony's land, and will sell it for {COUNT} silver, not being in a position to dig it up. There's no telling if the map is genuine without digging.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} pulls a scrap of old hide from {X_possessive} coat and spreads it out for {A_nameDef}. It's a map, with a mark scratched on a spot out on the colony's land. {X_nameDef} will part with it for {COUNT} silver, and swears it's genuine.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} shows {A_nameDef} an old survey printout with one spot circled in faded ink, right here on the colony's land. "Supply cache," {X_nameDef} says. "Pre-war. Never dug up." {X_nameDef} wants {COUNT} silver for it.

li.label: Buy it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The map is ours. {A_nameDef} heads out with a shovel to find the spot.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} digs where the map says, then digs again a few paces over, and finds nothing but stones in either hole. The silver is gone.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} folds the map away and goes looking for another buyer.

li.label: Have it checked first, then buy ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} looked the map over and found nothing wrong with it, though {X_nameDef} didn't enjoy being doubted. The colony bought it, and {A_nameDef} heads out with a shovel.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} held the hide up to the light, sniffed it, and nodded. The map is the colony's now, and {A_nameDef} heads out to find the spot.
[!lowtech] {B_nameDef} checked the survey marks against the colony's own maps, and they matched. {X_nameDef} took the silver with a sniff, and {A_nameDef} heads out with a shovel.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} turned the map over twice and handed it back: a fake, and not a good one. {X_nameDef} took offense at being found out, but the silver stays in the stores.

riskOutcomes.li: [b:past:scholar] {B_nameDef} has seen old maps before, and this one's ink was barely dry. {X_nameDef} packed it away in a temper, and the silver stays in the stores.

texts.li: [tribal] A runner of {ENEMY}, painted for war, has planted a spear outside the colony and named the price of peace: {COUNT} silver, by tomorrow. If it isn't paid, {ENEMY} will come and take it, along with whatever else they like.

[lowtech,!tribal] A herald of {ENEMY} rides up under a banner of truce, reads out a list of the colony's sins against no one in particular, and demands {COUNT} silver by tomorrow as the price of peace. Otherwise {ENEMY} will come and take it, and whatever else they like.

[!lowtech] The comms light up with a message from {ENEMY}: the colony is "under their protection" now, and protection costs {COUNT} silver. They'll wait a day for it. After that, they'll come and collect it themselves.

li.label: Pay the {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: The tribute is handed over. They take it and leave, and the colony goes back to work in a sour mood.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} haggle
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} argues them down to half the tribute, and they leave almost pleased with the deal.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} pushes too hard, and {ENEMY} take offense. They no longer want the tribute. A war party is coming instead, and soon.

li.label: {ENEMY} want their tribute
li.text: The haggling went badly. {ENEMY} have come to take what they asked for, and more.

li.label: Refuse
li.outcome: The answer is no. The colony has a day to get ready.

li.label: {ENEMY} want their tribute
li.text: The colony refused to pay. {ENEMY} have come to take it by force.
